notes_list.title: R/S Configuration — CIP Rules
notes_list.basic_overview: R/S descriptors are assigned using Cahn–Ingold–Prelog priority rules. They describe absolute configuration at a stereogenic center.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Prioritize directly attached atoms by atomic number; isotopes by mass. If tied, compare outward atom-by-atom until the first point of difference. Orient the lowest-priority group away and trace 1→2→3: clockwise R, anticlockwise S.
notes_list.examples: 2-butanol, lactic acid and substituted cyclohexanes provide common CIP practice.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: No medium; descriptor depends only on connectivity and 3D arrangement.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Assign priorities. 2. Orient group 4 away. 3. Trace 1→2→3. 4. Reverse if group 4 points toward the viewer. 5. Check multiple-bond duplicate-atom convention.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: CIP descriptors are not determined by optical rotation sign. R does not mean (+), and S does not mean (−).
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Frequently tested in multi-stereocenter structures and reaction products.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not assign priority by molecular mass of the whole group; compare atomic numbers at the first point of difference.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
